# Kapilasutta (Snp 2.6 (PTS Snp 49))

**ID:** Snp 2.6 (PTS Snp 49)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Kapilasutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kapilasutta* (also known as the *Dhammacariyasutta*; Snp 2.6, PTS Snp 49) is a poetic discourse preserved in the *Cūḷavagga* of the *Suttanipāta* [Norman 1997-2001]. Opening with an exposition on the life of righteousness and holiness as the gem of highest worth, the discourse highlights monastic practice as truly superior and warns practitioners to avoid companions harboring evil desires [Wijayaratna 1990; Sarada Thero].

Later Pali literature and commentaries frequently invoke the sutta. The *Vinaya* commentary (*Samantapāsādikā* 1098) and the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* (under the *Kapilamacchavatthu*, DhA iv 37 ff., citing this sutta at iv 42) record that the discourse was delivered in connection with the elder Yasoja and the five hundred sons of fishermen [Vinaya Pitaka vol 4 - Mahavagga]. In the commentary to *Dhammapada* verse 334, the Buddha is similarly recorded as preaching the *Kapila Sutta* in full to suit his audience's disposition [Sarada Thero]. The text is also cited in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 7.7.7, *Maṇiratanaṅgapañha*).
